overview: Two plant hormones with opposing roles in seed and bud dormancy — one wakes growth up, the other shuts it down.
genZNote: Gibberellin: 'time to wake up and grow.' Abscisic acid: 'time to shut down and wait it out.'

aspects.label: Effect on Dormancy
aspects.valueA: Breaks seed and bud dormancy, promoting germination and growth.
aspects.valueB: Induces and maintains seed/bud dormancy, and closes stomata under water stress.

aspects.label: Effect on Stomata
aspects.valueA: No major direct role in stomatal closure.
aspects.valueB: Directly triggers stomatal closure during drought stress.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Abscisic acid is the primary hormone responsible for closing stomata during water stress, a key drought-response fact.
overlay.commonMisconception: Abscisic acid is not just about dropping leaves (abscission) despite the name's origin — its main documented roles are dormancy and stress response, especially stomatal closure.
